contracts.commit_point: The ADK tool-execution step for the trader agent's place_order/modify_order call: a dict return from risk_manager_callback (callbacks.py:45-51, 58-64, 73-79, 90-97, 101-104) causes tool execution to be skipped before any order request is forwarded to the angel_one_mcp.server process; a None return (callbacks.py:35, 106) lets execution proceed.
contracts.declared_mechanism: LlmAgent(before_tool_callback=risk_manager_callback) on the trader agent (trader.py:41-48); the callback returns None to allow a call, or a {'status': 'REJECTED', 'reason': ...} dict which, per its documented contract, makes ADK skip tool execution and surface the dict as the tool result (callbacks.py:18-22).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Execution of a place_order/modify_order broker tool call where any of the following holds: (1) session daily P&L <= -max daily loss (callbacks.py:41-51); (2) for place_order only, open position count >= max open positions (callbacks.py:53-64); (3) current IST HH:MM >= square-off time and transactiontype/transaction_type is BUY (callbacks.py:66-79); (4) tradingsymbol/symbol ends with an equity suffix (-EQ/-BE/-BL/-AF/-IQ/-RL) or is not a CE/PE option symbol, when a symbol argument is present (callbacks.py:81-97); (5) the symbol prefix-matches a ban_list entry for today's date (callbacks.py:99-104, 109-123).
pending_binding_information: The skip-on-dict semantics of before_tool_callback are asserted only by the callback docstring (callbacks.py:20-22); the google.adk framework source is not supplied to confirm ADK skips execution (including for McpToolset tools) when a dict is returned.

Whether McpToolset-provided tools surface tool.name as exactly 'place_order'/'modify_order' to match ORDER_TOOLS is not demonstrated in supplied source; MCP tool wrapping/naming lives in the unsupplied SDK.
Real-time correctness of DAILY_PNL, OPEN_POSITIONS_COUNT, and APP_* state keys depends on updater code outside the supplied views.

The binding from 'tool execution skipped' to 'no order reaches the broker' relies on angel_one_mcp.server behavior that is not in supplied source; if the study classifies the protected effect by the broker-side mutation rather than the gated tool invocation, that stratum binding (network/external) is unverified.
The trader_instruction content (odta.prompts.trader) that would govern whether the agent reliably supplies symbol/transaction-type arguments is not supplied.
contracts.protected_operation: Tool dispatch of place_order or modify_order from the Angel One broker McpToolset during trader LlmAgent execution (tools=[broker_tools] + native_tools); non-order tools deliberately pass through unguarded (callbacks.py:29-35).
contracts.protected_resource: The Angel One broker order channel exposed via McpToolset(StdioConnectionParams(command='python', args=['-m','angel_one_mcp.server'])) (root_agent.py:15-35), together with the session-state counters and limit overrides (DAILY_PNL, OPEN_POSITIONS_COUNT, APP_MAX_DAILY_LOSS, APP_MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS, APP_SQUARE_OFF_TIME) and the ban_list table consulted by the guard.
contracts.protection_obligation: The risk_manager_callback, registered as before_tool_callback on the 'trader' LlmAgent that carries the Angel One broker MCP toolset, must reject any place_order/modify_order tool call that violates the daily-loss limit, the max-open-positions cap (new orders only), the post-square-off BUY restriction, the options-only symbol rule, or the F&O ban list; per the callback's documented contract a returned dict makes ADK skip tool execution, so the non-compliant order is never dispatched to the broker MCP server.
scope_limits: Guard fires only for tools named 'place_order' or 'modify_order' (callbacks.py:29-35); every other trader tool — including remaining Angel One MCP tools such as search_scrip and the paper-mode tools get_paper_positions/record_paper_trade — receives no risk checks.
The position-cap rule applies only to place_order; modify_order bypasses it (callbacks.py:53-57).

The square-off BUY check and the symbol/ban checks depend on args keys transactiontype/transaction_type and tradingsymbol/symbol; calls omitting these keys skip the corresponding checks (callbacks.py:66-104).

Enforcement inputs come from tool_context.state (DAILY_PNL, OPEN_POSITIONS_COUNT, APP_* overrides with constant defaults); the state-writer code and the odta.constants values are not in supplied source.
The ban check delegates to odta.db.connection.get_db_connection and a ban_list table using prefix matching (callbacks.py:109-123); neither the connection module nor table population is supplied.

The guard does not cover broker-side server configuration such as the DRY_RUN_MODE and MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY env passed to the MCP server (root_agent.py:26-32); any enforcement there lives in the unsupplied MCP server.
The time check compares IST HH:MM strings lexicographically against square_off_time; boundary behavior (equality counts as past square-off) is as coded and assumes a trusted clock.
